overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing non-qualifying topics in its June 27 executive session; no violation for the July 11 and 13 open-session discussions. Ordered compliance and release of redacted minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed matters in its June 27 executive session that were not on the notice or were not appropriate for executive session.
allegations.key_passage: None of those topics were appropriate for discussion in executive session, and the discussion in executive session therefore violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed reorganization of the Board at its July 11 and July 13 open meetings although those topics were not on the posted notices.
allegations.key_passage: On these facts, we do not find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed the process for placing topics on meeting notices (agenda creation) at July 11 and July 13 meetings without it being on the notices.
allegations.key_passage: Nor does the Law require the chair to add topics to a notice that are requested by fellow members of the public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Within 30 days, release the June 27 executive session minutes in their entirety and without redactions, except one paragraph summarizing discussion of two complaints about the Town Administrator, which may remain withheld until publication would no longer defeat the executive session's purpose.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
